abstract.t: Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs) make transparency logging part of certificate issuance, enabling Internet-scale deployments of short- lived certificates and large post-quantum signatures. In exchange, their security rests on the state, not just the keys, of the certification authority, its cosigners, and relying parties' update services. This document describes the architecture for deploying MTCs and defines the guarantees that a relying party can obtain when it accepts one. These cover who certified and who recorded the certificate, agreement among relying parties on each log entry, the enforcement of revoked ranges, and the validation of the relying party's own configuration. For each guarantee, we state which parties must behave as specified and which keys and state they must keep intact. Our Recommendations are not needed to interoperate, but they affect the guarantees a deployment achieves, especially against adversaries able to compromise a certification authority, a cosigner, or an update service.
